anki.deck.title: Import an Anki deck
anki.deck.intro: Already study this language in Anki? Import the deck and LWT will mark those words as known, so you do not have to reclassify them while reading. Export your deck from Anki with File → Export → Anki Deck Package (.apkg), including scheduling information.
anki.deck.creates_new_only: This creates new terms. It never changes terms you already have — importing the same deck twice is safe.
anki.deck.error_store_failed: Could not store the uploaded file.
anki.deck.error_no_notetypes: No notetypes found in this file — it may not be an Anki deck.
anki.deck.error_expired: That upload has expired. Please choose the file again.
anki.deck.mapping_intro: LWT cannot tell which field holds the word, or what language the deck is in — an .apkg does not record either. Choose them below.
anki.deck.status_derive_help: Cards you have known for {days} days or more become well known; younger cards get a learning status based on their interval; unstudied cards start at level 1; suspended cards become ignored.
anki.deck.status_fixed: Give every word the same status
anki.deck.all_empty_warning: Every note had an empty term field. The chosen field is probably not the one holding the word — go back and pick a different one.
anki.apkg.title: Import Anki .apkg
anki.apkg.due_dates_moved: Due dates set by hand in Anki
anki.apkg.unknown_notice_one: {count} note was not created by LWT, so nothing here matched it.
anki.apkg.unknown_notice_other: {count} notes were not created by LWT, so nothing here matched them.
anki.apkg.unknown_advice: This page only updates terms LWT exported in the first place. To bring these in as new terms, use Import an Anki deck, which asks which language they belong to.
anki.apkg.help: Notes from this file are matched to existing LWT terms by guid. Translations, romanizations, notes, and tags are updated; reviews you did in Anki are replayed into the term's schedule, and a due date you set by hand there is kept. Cards suspended in Anki demote learning-status terms to Ignored. Deleting a note in Anki does not delete the term here — an .apkg carries no record of deletions, so a term missing from the file is left alone rather than guessed at.
anki.apkg.settings_export_legacy: When you export, switch on Support older Anki versions (slower/larger files) — without it Anki writes a compressed collection this server cannot read, because PHP here has no zstd extension — and keep Include scheduling information on,
anki.apkg.settings_export: When you export, keep Include scheduling information switched on,
anki.apkg.settings_scheduling: without which your reviews stay behind in Anki.
anki.apkg.settings_import: Going the other way, tick Import any learning progress when you import an LWT deck into Anki, or Anki starts every card from scratch and discards the schedule this page exported.
anki.apkg.deck_notice_title: Importing a deck you built in Anki?
anki.apkg.deck_notice: This page only updates terms that LWT exported in the first place — a deck from Anki or AnkiWeb has nothing here to match against, so nothing would change. Use Import an Anki deck instead, which creates new terms and works out how well you know each word from Anki's own scheduling.
anki.sync.intro: Keep LWT and Anki in step, straight from Anki on this computer: no file to export or import. Reviews, translations, romanizations, notes, tags and suspensions travel both ways, and terms added on one side appear on the other.
anki.sync.step_addon_html: Install the AnkiConnect add-on, and keep Anki open.
anki.sync.step_export_html: Your cards must come from LWT: export them once with Export Language to Anki package (.apkg), so that each note carries its LwtId.
anki.sync.step_open: Click the button below. The first time, Anki asks whether to trust this page: accept.
anki.sync.rebuilt_one: {count} term had an older Anki review fitted into its history
anki.sync.rebuilt_other: {count} terms had older Anki reviews fitted into their history
anki.sync.skipped_one: {count} review skipped (ignored, well-known or deleted term)
anki.sync.skipped_other: {count} reviews skipped (ignored, well-known or deleted terms)
anki.sync.error_unreachable: Could not reach Anki at {url}. Is Anki open, with the AnkiConnect add-on installed?
anki.sync.error_denied: Anki refused access. Click the button again and accept the prompt in Anki.
anki.sync.how_html: Every change joins the other side as it happened: reviews in time order, so studying in both apps between two syncs gives the schedule you would have had in one; and fields, tags and suspensions by comparing each side with the last sync, so edits to different fields of a term both survive. Syncing again is safe: what either side already has is skipped. A term in a language with an LWT:: deck in Anki is added there, and a note you add to such a deck becomes a term.
anki.sync.hosted_html: If LWT runs on another server, your browser may ask for permission to reach Anki on this computer, or block it; allowing local network access for this site fixes that. The .apkg file round trip works everywhere.
anki.sync.fsrs_html: With FSRS on in Anki, Anki also keeps its own memory estimate for each card, which reviews sent from LWT do not update: AnkiConnect cannot write it. The due dates are right; to bring the estimates in line too, run Optimize in Anki's deck options now and then.

anki.sync.notes_to_anki_other: {count} changes sent to Anki (fields, tags or suspensions)

anki.sync.added_to_lwt_other: {count} notes added in Anki became terms
